correctness.rationale: Baigent et al. 2023 Theorem 3.4 yields convergence to some fixed point for r=s=2; a positive-invasion argument excludes all but the coexistence equilibrium when 0<gamma<1. The exact mean/imbalance update contracts the imbalance and admits a weighted backward-scalar-shadowing contraction, producing a smooth asymptotic phase and exceptional strong-stable graph. The scalar second-iterate expansion has exact cubic coefficient -1/3 and quintic +1/30, yielding inverse-square increment 2/3+(4/15)U^{-1}+O(U^{-3/2}), finite centered logarithmic constant and universal 2/5 log correction. Analytic nonzero Jacobian and inverse-function locality prove the exceptional preimage union null. Graph invariance fixes curvature -gamma(1-gamma)/(1-2gamma+5gamma^2). Symbolic exact expansions and four high-precision trajectory samples passed; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: At r=s=2 the symmetric planar Ricker coexistence point has the natural neutral multiplier -1, so convergence alone supplies no speed. The theorem gives the exact leading and subleading all-orbit relaxation law, distinguishes a measure-zero exponentially convergent invariant preimage family from the generic algebraic class, and computes its genuinely parameter-dependent geometric curvature. The exact 2/5 logarithmic coefficient and full-positive-quadrant scope address concrete long-time model behavior absent from qualitative stability and numerical bifurcation diagrams; no broader parameter or topology claim is made.
